summary: Oregon Department of Forestry secondary lookout tower, 70 ft, built 1932 per a district report; listed as Removed or Gone. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Secondary lookout tower, 70 feet tall, on the Scoggin-Sein Creek ridge (sec 34, T1N R5W)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it Removed and firelookout.com marks it Gone. No source gives a removal date or method.

events.note: Secondary lookout tower, 70 feet, per a Tillamook District annual report quoted on Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com dates its crow's nest to the 1930s
Activated October 19, 1942; Portland Filter Center named on the record

evidence.supports: 1932 construction of a secondary lookout tower, 70 feet tall, in section 34, T1N R5W
evidence.quote: 1932: Constructed secondary lookout tower 70 feet in height on Scoggin-Sein Creek ridge in sec 34 T1N R5W

evidence.supports: Activation date October 19, 1942, with the Portland Filter Center named
Record is listed under the Oregon Department of Forestry
Forest Lookouts marks the tower Removed
firelookout.com marks it Gone and describes a 1930s crow's nest

Managing agency given as Oregon Dept. of Forestry on the firelookout.com listing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1932 district annual report describing a secondary lookout tower 70 feet tall. firelookout.com describes a 1930s crow's nest. The record keeps the 1932 tower description because it gives a date and height, and it marks the crow's nest description as unreconciled.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both thin. The 1932 entry is a quote from a Tillamook District annual report as printed on the Forest Lookouts page; the report itself was not read. The firelookout.com page gives county, distance and status but no elevation or height. Baseline Ridge is not in the FFLOS Oregon county listing for Washington County, so no FFLOS record was used. The brief's access 'unknown' is left out because no source states an access rule. Removal date and method are not documented. The 1932 tower description and the firelookout.com crow's nest description disagree; the record keeps the tower and notes the disagreement.
